sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: An injured Tigst Assefa crossed the finish line to win the Berlin Marathon on Sunday. She led the race and looked set to break the world record before fading in the final stages due to a tendon issue. Despite slowing down, she still won with the third-fastest time in history and broke her own Berlin course record. Guye Adola won the men's race, and the top five women's finishers were all from Ethiopia.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Assefa achieved the third-fastest time in history and improved upon her previous course record and London Marathon time, despite suffering a painful injury towards the end of the race.
